set.tagline: A space MMO survives its official servers by handing the universe to its players.
set.description: Star Conflict is a free Windows space combat game by Star Gem Inc. Its official online servers closed in October 2026. The Steam client now includes a local server component for the community-operated edition, with PvP, PvE, and exploration modes that may differ from the original service.

qualityBar.verdict: The ships still have a fight in them; the hard part now is choosing whose community universe to trust.

set.longDescription:
Star Conflict used to be the sort of space game that assumed an official server would always be waiting. You built a fleet, chose a ship for a role, and flew into PvP battles, PvE missions, or open space. In October 2026, Gaijin shut those servers down. The game did not disappear, but the way you play it changed. The free Steam release now includes a client and a local server component for a community-operated edition. That handoff is the defining fact of the game today, and it should be the first thing a new pilot knows.

There is still plenty to like in the cockpit. Interceptors reward speed and nerve; heavier ships can hold a line or support a team. Weapons, modules, and equipment let you tune a ship for a job rather than simply climb a single ladder of bigger numbers. The original game accumulated a broad fleet and many maps over years of updates. The autonomous version keeps those ships and locations available, but Gaijin warns that particular modes, content, and progression may work differently from the former official service. Treat it as a preserved world with a different front door, not a promise that every old account and item will come back.

To enter that world, install the Windows client through Steam, start its local server component, then connect the client. Friends can join an independently operated server or one you run yourself. The official instructions cover the server setup; it is more involved than pressing Play on a normal MMO. Existing Gaijin account progression and purchases do not transfer to community servers. A server operator may ask for a separate account, so choose the host and read its privacy information before registering.

There is a crucial boundary for PlayBound. Gaijin allows noncommercial community servers under its Community Edition terms and explicitly restricts monetization and redistribution of the client or server files. We cannot treat that as permission to include Star Conflict in a paid PlayBound hosting plan, mirror its binaries, or claim a one-click PlayBound dedicated service. The game supports multiplayer and local server play in principle; PlayBound has not verified a compatible hosted recipe or automatic party connection. Its current PC listing also does not establish a verified controller setup, so we will not advertise one.

We are keeping Star Conflict in Draft while we check whether the autonomous version offers an experience that meets our bar. The idea of an online universe carried forward by its players is compelling. So is the prospect of returning to a favorite ship and choosing your own battle. The setup, trust, and licensing limits are part of the experience now. A useful game page needs to explain those limits as clearly as it explains the flight.
set.whyWePickedIt: We are reviewing Star Conflict because its community-operated edition gives a long-running space combat game a path after official service closure. Its ships and roles still suggest good team play. We need a verified setup and a clear account of the noncommercial server terms before recommending or hosting it through PlayBound.
set.thatOneThing: The official servers vanished, but your favorite ship can still launch if someone keeps a universe running.

installSteps.text: Install the free Star Conflict client through its official Steam page. Gaijin says the community client remains available exclusively through Steam; do not use third-party client mirrors.

Follow the official Community Edition setup guide to start the included local server component, then launch the client and connect to that server. This is a manual setup, not a verified PlayBound one-click server install.

firstPlaySteps.text: Start with a local or trusted community server. Expect separate progression from the former official service and check which modes that server actually offers.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use the included server component or connect to an independently operated community server, following Gaijin's Community Edition instructions. Existing Gaijin account progression does not transfer.

PlayBound has not verified an automatic party connection or a paid hosted server recipe for this edition. Gaijin's terms allow noncommercial community operation and restrict server monetization and file redistribution.

bestFor: Space-combat players willing to set up or choose a trusted community server
Groups who enjoy ship roles and team battles
Former pilots curious about the autonomous edition
notFor: Anyone expecting their old official account progression to transfer
Players who want a verified one-click PlayBound server
Anyone looking for a browser game

faq.a: Yes, in the community-operated edition. Gaijin closed its official servers in October 2026, but the free Steam client includes a local server component.

faq.q: Can I install it from PlayBound's mirror?
faq.a: No. Gaijin says the client is available exclusively through Steam and its Community Edition terms restrict redistribution of the files.

faq.q: Can PlayBound host a server for my subscription?
faq.a: Not under the current noncommercial Community Edition terms. PlayBound has no verified paid-hosting recipe for this game.

faq.q: Will my old ships and purchases carry over?
faq.a: No. Gaijin says former official progression, items, and entitlements cannot be transferred to community servers.
The current Steam system requirements list Windows 10. PlayBound has not verified Mac or Linux builds for the autonomous edition.
PlayBound has not verified a controller configuration for the current Windows community edition.

launcherInstall.note: Steam provides the free Community Edition client and included server component. Local server setup is manual; do not mirror or monetize server files.
